case: PostgreSQL custom enum[] XLSX re-import through Gnumeric
contract: The native enum[] includes literal NULL, empty text, Unicode, comma, quote, markup, formula-shaped =1+1, backslash and SQL NULL labels.
The native oracle checks enum[] type, array JSON and array_send bytes; rebinding reproduces both JSON and wire bytes.

The XLSX writer stores the complete array as a text cell without a formula. SQL-file replay preserves it under all four standard_conforming_strings/backslash_quote combinations and leaves the sibling array intact.
Gnumeric preserves the exact array literal as a text cell through XLSX/ODS/XLSX re-save, including the formula-shaped label.

native_export_test.command: rtk proxy env BOOKIEE_XLSX_REIMPORT_ARTIFACT=<absolute-evidence-dir>/source.xlsx cargo test --locked -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration array_contract::value_contract_custom_enum_array_file_exports_preserve_labels -- --include-ignored --exact --test-threads=1

steps: Install Gnumeric in the pinned Debian container.
Convert source.xlsx to gnumeric-roundtrip.ods, then the ODS to gnumeric-roundtrip.xlsx.

consumer_assertions.method: Python standard-library ZIP/XML checks exact A2 array text, requires string cell types and rejects formulas in source and both re-saved workbooks.
consumer_assertions.result: Full enum[] text, including =1+1 and SQL NULL distinction, preserved.

remaining: Other spreadsheet applications, enum array shapes and the broader B3 matrix remain open.
